title: An email whose domain isn't the account's own predicts a bounce or the wrong person
hypothesis: Emails that passed enrichment were the right people at the right firms.
change: Compared each lead's email domain with its firm's domain across the three active audiences.

oracle.baseline: lifetime bounce rate before the fix

result: 102 of 481 Qube leads (89 of 355 Vertocol, 47 of 214 Ivy) had an email domain that didn't match the firm, next to a 27% bounce rate and a wrong-person reply. Examples: an Accel partner at an unrelated domain, a firm name on a gmail address.
next_decision: Exclude mismatched emails from every audience; count an email as verified only when its domain is the account's own or its parent's.
check: Run `chewbacca gtme lesson verified-email --email-domain D --status S --brand-domain B [--parent P]` on every found email; a valid email at another domain doesn't count.
scope: Any list where emails came from enrichment rather than the person. Personal domains (gmail) are a mismatch for a firm contact.
